issues.description: is_registered mutation on shared TritonLoraConfig is not thread-safe and races under concurrent first-use
issues.detail: TritonLoraConfig instances are shared across all concurrent requests via TritonModelMetadata.lora_configs. _create_trtllm_generate_request reads is_registered, loads weights from disk, sends them, and sets is_registered=True with no synchronization. Two concurrent first-time requests for the same LoRA will both observe is_registered=False, both load and send weights; conversely a request can flip the flag to True before another in-flight request has actually reached the backend, causing later requests to omit lora_weights/lora_config before the backend has cached them. Fix with a per-config asyncio.Lock with check-after-acquire, send weights idempotently every time, or split immutable spec from a separately-synchronized registration registry.

issues.description: lora_task_id assignment is unstable across reloads/repos and has no documented invariant
issues.detail: lora_task_id starts at 1 per call to _parse_lora_configs and increments in dict-iteration order across repo_paths. The TRT-LLM backend caches by task_id; if multi_lora.json is edited, a model is reloaded, or two model repos both define LoRAs, task_ids can shift or collide while the backend still holds the old mapping. The invariant tying (lora_name, weights) to a stable task_id is never stated or enforced. Use a server-scoped counter, a content-derived hash, or an explicit task_id field in multi_lora.json, and document the lifetime/scope.

issues.description: _get_lora_config can NoneType-crash and contradicts its declared return type
issues.detail: self.model_metadata.get(model_name) can return None and the next line dereferences model_metadata.lora_configs, raising AttributeError instead of a ClientError. The signature is annotated `-> TritonLoraConfig` but the function also returns None when lora_name is None or lora_configs is None, so callers branch on None despite the non-Optional annotation. Make the signature honest (Optional[TritonLoraConfig]) and handle the missing-metadata case explicitly with a ClientError.

issues.description: Blocking np.load of LoRA weights runs synchronously inside the async request hot path
issues.detail: _create_trtllm_generate_request calls np.load on model.lora_weights.npy and model.lora_config.npy from within an async coroutine on the first request for each LoRA. This blocks the event loop, pays variable disk-I/O latency per cold path, and under the is_registered race pays it N times. Load and cache the parsed ndarrays once at _parse_lora_configs time (or via a registry behind a thread executor) and attach them to TritonLoraConfig so the request path only references already-materialized values.

issues.description: lora_config_path is shadowed inside the loop, clobbering the outer multi_lora.json path
issues.detail: In _parse_lora_configs, lora_config_path is first bound to `<version>/multi_lora.json`, then rebound inside the TRT-LLM branch of the per-LoRA loop to `os.path.join(lora_path, 'model.lora_config.npy')`. On subsequent iterations of the outer repo_paths loop or future maintenance, the outer meaning is gone. Rename the inner variable (e.g., lora_config_npy_path / lora_adapter_config_path) so the two distinct concepts do not share a name.

issues.description: Bare `except Exception` in _parse_lora_configs swallows real errors and returns None
issues.detail: The outer try around the multi_lora.json read catches every non-ServerError exception, prints a traceback to stdout, and returns None — which the caller treats as 'this model has no LoRAs.' A malformed JSON file, permission error, OSError on a network mount, or KeyError inside our own code becomes indistinguishable from 'no LoRA configured.' Narrow the except to JSONDecodeError/OSError, propagate as ServerError with context, or return a tagged failure so the caller can distinguish 'disabled' from 'broken.'

issues.description: Return type annotation on _parse_lora_configs is stale and incorrect
issues.detail: Signature reads `-> None | List[tuple[str, str]]` but the function returns `Optional[List[TritonLoraConfig]]`. The annotation is left over from the previous _get_vllm_lora_names shape and misleads both readers and type checkers. Update to `Optional[List[TritonLoraConfig]]`.

issues.description: LoRA lookups use O(L) list comprehensions where a dict by name would suffice
issues.detail: _validate_chat_request, _validate_completion_request, and _get_lora_config each independently scan metadata.lora_configs with `lora_name not in [c.name for c in metadata.lora_configs]` or equivalent. Three duplicated linear scans with three potentially-divergent error messages where the underlying data structure should be Dict[str, TritonLoraConfig] (or augmented with a name->config index built once at parse time). Collapse the call-sites behind one helper returning Optional[TritonLoraConfig].

issues.description: Stray `print(f"backend: {backend}")` debug statement in the per-LoRA parse loop
issues.detail: Inside _parse_lora_configs a debug print fires once per LoRA per model on every metadata refresh, dumping unstructured output to stdout in production. Remove it, or convert to a single structured logger.debug call outside the loop.

issues.description: `print(traceback.format_exc())` added to three FastAPI routers bypasses logging configuration
issues.detail: chat.py, completions.py, and embeddings.py each gain `import traceback` and `print(traceback.format_exc())` in exception handlers (including for the unrelated embeddings endpoint). This is logging-by-print: it bypasses the application logger, log levels, structured fields, and log rotation, and it duplicates the same block at three sites. Route through `logger.exception` with a stable logger name, or remove. Ideally split the router error-handling change out of the LoRA feature PR.

issues.description: is_registered: Optional[bool] = False is a misleading type annotation
issues.detail: TritonLoraConfig.is_registered is declared Optional[bool] with default False but is only ever read/written as a plain bool. None is unreachable and meaningless. Drop the Optional — annotations should mean what they say. Better still, eliminate the field in favor of an explicit registration registry whose state lives where the truth lives.

issues.description: Backend dispatch silently routes unknown backends into the TRT-LLM LoRA path
issues.detail: _get_model_metadata passes `backend if self.backend is None else self.backend` to _parse_lora_configs, which uses `if backend == 'vllm': ... else: # assume TRT-LLM`. An ensemble, python, or otherwise unknown backend falls through to the TRT-LLM branch and only avoids crashing because multi_lora.json happens to be absent. The CLI-declared global backend can also silently override per-model backend. Dispatch explicitly on `backend in {'vllm', 'tensorrtllm'}` and reject (or no-op) unknown backends rather than defaulting them into the tensor-loading path.

issues.description: TritonLoraConfig conflates immutable spec with mutable runtime state and backend-specific fields
issues.detail: The dataclass mixes name (common), task_id/path (TRT-LLM only), and is_registered (mutable runtime cache state) into one record shared across backends and across concurrent requests. Split into a frozen TritonLoraSpec (or VllmLoraConfig/TrtLlmLoraConfig variants) plus a separate registration registry — that removes the race window, makes the type system honest about which fields apply to which backend, and clarifies that the TRT-LLM cache protocol belongs in a thin backend adapter rather than the request builder.

issues.description: _parse_lora_configs complects discovery, validation, and task-id allocation across two backends
issues.detail: The renamed function fuses (1) discover LoRA names from multi_lora.json, (2) validate that .npy files exist on disk, (3) allocate task_ids for TRT-LLM, and branches on backend with two largely disjoint code paths. Split into _parse_vllm_lora_configs and _parse_trtllm_lora_configs sharing only a small directory-resolution helper, and move task-id allocation into an explicit LoraRegistry abstraction.

issues.description: Tests do not assert TRT-LLM-specific postconditions of _parse_lora_configs
issues.detail: test_parse_lora_configs invokes the function for both backends but only asserts the shared ValueError path and discards the parsed result. The TRT-LLM-specific contract (ServerError when .npy files are missing, monotonically assigned task_ids, correct TritonLoraConfig contents) is unverified. Add assertions on the returned list and split the parametrization so backend-specific behavior is tested independently.

issues.description: FIXME sed patches dims in config.pbtxt without a tracked issue or pinned TRT-LLM version
issues.detail: qa/L0_openai/test.sh runs `sed -i 's/dims: \[ -1, 3 \]/dims: \[ -1, 4 \]/'` on tensorrt_llm and tensorrt_llm_bls config.pbtxt files with a bare FIXME. There is no linked upstream ticket and no termination condition; a future TRT-LLM update will silently break or silently succeed. Link an issue and/or pin the TRT-LLM version this workaround targets.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a NEEDS-WORK verdict. The feature itself (extending LoRA support from vLLM to TRT-LLM in the OpenAI frontend) lands real capability, but the underlying state machine has not had its invariants stated and breaks under concurrency. Three P0 issues are unanimously flagged: the is_registered flag is mutated on a shared TritonLoraConfig from async handlers with no synchronization (racing concurrent first-use requests can either double-send weights or skip them before the backend has cached them); lora_task_id assignment is unstable across reloads and repo orderings with no documented invariant tying name to id; and _get_lora_config will NoneType-crash on unknown model_name while its return type lies about Optional. Beyond those, the panel agrees on a cluster of P1 hygiene and structural issues: synchronous np.load on the async request path, a shadowed lora_config_path local, a stale return-type annotation, a bare except Exception that silently disables LoRA, debug prints (`print(f"backend: ...")` and traceback prints across three routers), O(L) list comprehensions where a dict-by-name belongs, and ambiguous backend dispatch. The recommended fixes are: extract an explicit LoraRegistry ADT with stated synchronization and stability invariants, split immutable spec from mutable registration state, move weight loading to parse time, replace the catch-all with typed failures, fix the type annotations, switch lookups to a name-keyed dict, route exceptions through the logger, and split the unrelated router/docs changes into their own PRs.
